title: Starting on drums, his mother's objections and the hocked snare drum
summary: Hazel tells how his father bought his snare drum, later pawned it, and how he found it again at a marching club and began professional playing at about 14.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: What are some of the other bands that you played with back around?
Well, I played the, after Hardy, after, after we moved on this side of the river. My dad was, used to drink quite a bit. See, mother didn't want me to play music at all.
I was gonna ask first of all, just how old you were when you started with the drums? Had you played anything else at all first? That was a very good thing.

No, no, that was, that was, on account of my dad being there. Yeah. He bought me, first he bought me a snare drum. You see? Mm-hmm. And then I just, just played the snare drum. Like I told you, every time they'd come running for Rag Baby, well I'd have to take his place. And then, and then the parades. You had your own snare drum then you got. My dad bought me a snare drum. Incidentally, later on he hocked it. And, and I went to, there was a place down here on, down around Napoleon Avenue called the Mysterious Babies. It was a marching club, like the Jefferson City Buzzers, you know. And I walk in there one night, I was, I guess I was around 14, 15 years old, I walk in there one night to this dance. And there was an old yawk snare drum. They haven't made any of those in years and years. They made, they made drums and they made horns too. But this, this was the snare drum and, and, and, and I had a mark on it. See, and I walk up and I'm, naturally go right by the van. And, uh, I see my snare drum. See, so right away I go, I go, I said, I said, where you got this snare drum? And they said, they didn't call them snare drums, they called them Kittle drums. I said, where you get the Kittle drums? He said, I bought that off a man. I said, what man? I said, who you bought it off? He said, I bought it off a man by the name Mr. Hazel. I'll give him seven dollars for this drum. See, so I said, well, that's it. So I come home and I asked the old man about it. He had been on, on, on, on the tail, you know. That's where, that's where, that's where they went, the snare drum. So I didn't, uh, I didn't start playing professional until I was around 14. And I bought a set of drums. And I played with, oh, three or four different bands. A couple of bands over the river. And, uh, Martha Boswell and, and, and Connie and, and, uh, that. Used to have a little, they used to have a little trio. And I used to go, they lived on, down here on Camp Street and used to go by their house and play.
